Issued at 208 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Today-Tonight...Hazardous beach and marine conditions persist today 
as rough surf and a high risk of life-threatening rip currents 
remain at area beaches. Entering the surf is strongly discouraged! 
Northeast winds let up just a bit as the pressure gradient weakens 
slightly over central Florida and the adjacent Atlantic waters. As a 
low pressure system gradually moves away from the Mid Atlantic coast 
through tonight, drier air will filter south across Florida. Even 
where PW values remain near 1" along the Martin County coast, model 
soundings show the near-surface layer and every space in between 
above 850mb as very dry. A few CAM solutions try to develop 
extremely shallow marine-layer showers that approach the Treasure 
Coast from time to time, mainly this afternoon. With little model 
support overall, decided to keep mentionable rain chances out of the 
official forecast. However, a sprinkle or isolated, fast-moving 
shower would not be totally surprising across the far southern 
coast. 

Forecast high temperatures remain 2-4 degrees below normal in the 
upper 70s/low 80s. Drier air and the northeast breeze will make for 
rather pleasant outdoor conditions. Tonight, temps may cool a degree 
or two more in spots as onshore flow weakens to 5-10 mph inland, 10-
15 mph at the coast.

Wednesday-Thursday...High pressure remains in place over our area 
through the mid/latter portion of the week, while a cold front moves 
through the Northeast and Mid Atlantic regions. This forces an old 
occluded front and strong low pressure system over the western 
Atlantic seaward Thursday into Friday. A modest pressure gradient 
around the southern periphery of the surface high reinforces onshore 
flow through this period, generally 5-10 mph inland (10-15 mph 
coast) each night and 10-15+ mph each day. Gusts will peak 20-25 
mph, especially closer to the coast. Occasional gusts above 30 mph 
are a possibility along the Volusia/north Brevard coast Wednesday, 
highlighted by NBE probabilities of 30-50%. Slightly lower probs for 
30+ mph gusts are present along the entire coast Thursday.

PW climb above 1" for most of the area Wednesday, allowing for more 
marine stratocu to develop, push onshore, and bring with it a chance 
for showers. QPF remains light, generally 0.05-0.10" for those 
locations that do see rain (mainly along the coast). Drier air makes 
another push south early Thursday, suppressing low rain chances from 
north to south on Thursday. Most of the area will stay dry Thursday. 
Temps are fairly status-quo, reaching the low 80s Wednesday and 
cooling a degree or two Thursday into the upper 70s/low 80s. 
Locations north of I-4 have the best potential at reaching the upper 
50s each night, especially Thursday night. 

Friday-Monday...A residual front, stretching from Cuba toward the 
southeastern Bahamas, becomes a fulcrum of sorts late this week into 
the weekend for low pressure to develop. Several surface-850mb 
reflections are apparent in medium range guidance along this front, 
albeit disorganized and generally elongated in appearance. High 
pressure over southern Canada and the Northeast U.S. pivots a bit 
farther south as it strengthens into the weekend. This really helps 
to tighten the pressure gradient over our area (00z guidance EC/GFS 
show a 8-10mb delta between JAX/MIA) and give a boost to northeast 
winds. Sustained winds Friday afternoon of 15-20 mph could reach as 
high as 20-30 mph Saturday and Sunday. Wind Advisories, especially 
along the immediate coast, will be given strong consideration if 
these model solutions hold. Another indicator of this stronger wind 
event is the ECMWF EFI, whose scores of 0.7 to 0.85 (Saturday to 
Sunday, respectively) signal an unusually gusty 48 hours. Strong 
winds could even continue into Monday before the high starts to 
weaken Tuesday and beyond. In short, this weekend will be windy and 
not friendly to any outdoor decorations/items that are not well-
secured. 

This uptick in winds will also lead to another hazardous coastal 
event with beach erosion, rough surf, and dangerous rip currents, 
beginning as soon Friday. Rain chances are less certain with the 
greatest confidence in measurable precip south of Cape Canaveral 
through Monday. The best chance for onshore-moving showers may 
arrive Saturday as a brief surge of 1.2"+ PW pushes onshore from the 
Atlantic. Otherwise, coastal showers at night will have a tendency 
to push farther inland during the daylight hours. Generally, 20-40% 
rain chances at the coast (up to 50% south of Sebastian) and 15-30% 
inland...with the exception of some higher chances on Saturday (50-
70% at the coast). More clouds will be in the mix at the coast with 
more sunshine across the interior. Daytime temperatures stay rather 
steady (upper 70s/low 80s), but overnight lows warm into the mid 
60s/low 70s due to stronger onshore flow.
